svg.title: How the block changed
svg.desc: Top, the five memory edits of sessions 1 and 2. Session 1, second message: memory_insert, one paragraph. Session 2: memory_replace with an old_string of 253 characters, the whole block, of which 26 characters changed: 'strict vegetarian (8 years' became 'pescatarian (recently started eating fish'; two memory_insert calls of one line each; and memory_replace with an old_string of 438 characters, the whole block, of which nothing changed: one sentence of 52 characters was appended. Bottom, the block after session 2, with the replaced phrase, the two inserted lines and the appended sentence marked. Three notes: the earlier value is gone; 'about a month ago' became 'recently'; 'Lena can't eat shellfish' became 'Lena has a shellfish allergy'.
svg.text: The agent's five edits in sessions 1 and 2. Both replaces sent the whole block as the text to find, although each changed a
small part of it, or nothing.
for each replace: the text sent, to scale, and the part that changed
inserted 253 characters: one paragraph, everything from both messages
old_string: 253 characters, the whole block; 26 changed
inserted 93 characters: one line, the move to Kreuzberg
inserted 75 characters: one line, Lena and Jonas
old_string: 438 characters, the whole block; none changed
to append one sentence of 52 characters
) with a severe, anaphylactic peanut allergy. They
are planning a dinner in Berlin for their sister's visit. They prefer Indian cuisine, specifically paneer
dishes, and have a budget of around 40 euros per person.
They recently moved to Kreuzberg (May), so restaurants within walking distance are preferred.
The user's sister, Lena, is visiting in the autumn with her partner, Jonas.
inserted, or appended by a replace
The earlier value is gone: nothing says the user was vegetarian, or until when.
“About a month ago” became “recently”; “(8 years)” was dropped.
“Lena can't eat shellfish” became “Lena has a shellfish allergy”.
